title: Runbook (finite-settlement-algebra pre-settled step sequence; κ < ω)
description: Regime: finite-settlement-algebra (settling-regime record, κ < ω). Derivation from CLAUDE.md four-regime grammar: a runbook is a finite, pre-determined sequence of steps — execution-settled before its trigger fires (per lab runbook.md: 'The runbook's step sequence is in Fix(Δ_t): execution-settled before the trigger fires'). A finite list-of-steps IS a finite artifact, sitting in the strict-finite regime. Individual STEPS may invoke morphisms in any regime (an aperiodic-articulating LLM call, a transfinite-predicating fiber composition, a Scott-continuous-positing stance commit, or a finite-settling closure step); each step's regime is tagged in the step's optional `regime` field. The runbook RECORD itself is finite-settlement-algebra; the steps it sequences span regimes — that's the structural definition of a runbook as cross-regime composition orchestrator. Per platform-opener (pre-stabilization but structurally correct): runbooks are entities; runbook execution is dispatched, ticked, and witnessed like any other entity.

regime.description: Declares the runbook record's regime (always finite-settlement-algebra; the record is a finite step sequence).
The regime the step's invoked morphism inhabits. Steps span regimes; the runbook record itself is finite-settlement-algebra.
